clue.text: Briefly observe raucous cries of birds of North Europe

parts.note: to scan is to look over quickly
a din is a loud clamour
avian means relating to birds

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher glances at the noisy calling of northern European birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Norway, Sweden and Denmark make up the northern European region the adjective describes.

clue.text: Ship to mark position: it's not part of main action

definitions.text: it's not part of main action

parts.note: a sub is a submarine, a kind of ship
to plot is to mark a position on a chart

explanation.surface: A navigator charts a ship's position, a side issue away from the main battle.
explanation.definitionFit: A secondary storyline runs alongside the main narrative of a play or novel.

clue.text: Hazy in the middle, river is blue

indicators.note: the central letters of the word hazy are taken, dropping its first and last

parts.note: the Ure is a river in Yorkshire, England

explanation.surface: A misty river reflects a blue sky.
explanation.definitionFit: A bright sky-blue colour, a word used in poetry and heraldry.

clue.text: Deplore catching cold in repeated storms

indicators.note: catching means one piece holds another inside it
storms suggests violent upheaval, so the word repeated is thrown into a new order

parts.note: C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: Someone laments catching a chill during one storm after another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'storms' rearranges REPEATED into DEPREATE, and 'catching' puts C inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To deprecate is to express disapproval of something, much as deploring does.

clue.text: Record a tiny piece of music

explanation.surface: A tiny scrap of music gets recorded.
explanation.definitionFit: To jot something down is to record it; a single sounded pitch is the smallest unit of a melody.

clue.text: Wine priest lifted to lips

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifted means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: Rev is short for Reverend, a priest's title
the lips stand for the mouth by association

explanation.surface: A priest raises a glass of wine to his lips.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortified wine flavoured with herbs, used in a martini.

clue.text: Scots town expels the Spanish from prayer

indicators.note: expels means some letters are thrown out of the longer word

parts.note: the Angelus is a Catholic devotional prayer
el is the Spanish word for the

explanation.surface: A Scottish town bans Spaniards from public worship.
explanation.walkthrough: Angus is a historic county and council area in eastern Scotland; the clue calls it a town.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish region north of Dundee, here loosely called a town.

clue.text: Some such thing needed for wedding (not one's own)

definitions.text: Some such thing needed for wedding

explanation.surface: A bride's traditional good-luck items include one that belongs to someone else.
explanation.walkthrough: The rhyme says a bride needs something old, something new, something borrowed, something blue.
explanation.definitionFit: The wedding rhyme lists a lent item among a bride's charms; anything lent is taken from someone else temporarily.

clue.text: Practice of lecherous old huntsman?

parts.note: one archaic word means both sexual indulgence and the pursuit of game, so a lustful old hunter practises it in both senses

explanation.definitionFit: The archaic word covers both lustful pursuit and hunting game with hounds.

clue.text: Signal to leave miserable cell

parts.note: feeling blue means feeling sad
peter is old criminal slang for a prison cell

explanation.surface: A gloomy prisoner is told he may leave his cell.
explanation.walkthrough: The Blue Peter is a blue-and-white flag a ship flies when about to sail.
explanation.definitionFit: A naval flag hoisted in port to show a vessel is about to depart.

clue.text: The maxim of an international banker

explanation.surface: A global financier's favourite saying.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'gnomes of Zurich' is a nickname for Swiss bankers.
explanation.definitionFit: A pithy saying or aphorism; Swiss financiers were nicknamed the little men of Zurich.

clue.text: First violinist announced these German songs

indicators.note: announced means the word is spoken, so its sound counts rather than its spelling

parts.note: the leader of an orchestra is its principal first violin

explanation.surface: The principal violinist introduces a set of German songs.
explanation.definitionFit: Romantic art songs for voice and piano, as by Schubert.

clue.text: Analyse tricks? Yes

parts.note: cons are swindles or tricks
true is an affirmation, like yes

explanation.surface: Someone asked whether to analyse the tricks answers yes.
explanation.definitionFit: To interpret or parse a sentence is to work out its meaning.

clue.text: Eastern prince in town to see Roman emperor

indicators.note: in means one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: TN is an abbreviation for town
a raja is an Indian prince

explanation.surface: An Indian prince visits a town to meet a Roman emperor.
explanation.definitionFit: Emperor of Rome from 98 to 117, famous for his column.

clue.text: Comprehensive college?

parts.note: a college for everyone would admit every person; one Oxford college's name says just that

explanation.definitionFit: An Oxford college whose name, read literally, sounds as if it takes everybody.

clue.text: Pack to take a passage — get one free?

parts.note: to stow is to pack away
a way is a path or passage

explanation.surface: A traveller packs to take a voyage and wonders about getting a free ticket.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: someone who hides aboard gets a free passage.
explanation.definitionFit: A hidden passenger travels without paying a fare.

clue.text: The solution is to conceal one's defects, without conceding anything

definitions.text: The solution is to conceal one's defects

explanation.surface: Advice on covering up one's faults while admitting nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A lime solution brushed over walls hides blemishes; a sporting rout where the loser scores nothing.

clue.text: It'S a small world

parts.note: the saying is read literally as a land of tiny people, from Swift's satire of Gulliver's travels

explanation.definitionFit: The island of tiny people in Gulliver's Travels is a literal miniature realm.

clue.text: Terse report of gunshot victim's condition?

explanation.surface: A short news item on the state of a man who was shot.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word as 'bullet in', the state of someone shot.
explanation.definitionFit: A short news update or official statement; split in two it describes a wounded person still carrying the round.

clue.text: Graduate, jolly uncouth chap

parts.note: BA is a Bachelor of Arts, a graduate
boon, as in boon companion, means jolly or convivial

explanation.surface: A cheerful graduate who is nonetheless a boor.
explanation.definitionFit: A primate, used figuratively for a crude, oafish man.

clue.text: Slag taking drink about noon

indicators.note: about means one piece goes round the other

parts.note: cider is an apple drink

explanation.surface: Someone insults another while having a drink at midday.
explanation.definitionFit: Clinker or ash left after burning coal, like the waste from smelting.

clue.text: Lack of warmth is a limitation

explanation.surface: Coldness of manner is a drawback.
explanation.definitionFit: Reticence or coolness of manner; a restriction or qualification, as in accepting without condition.

clue.text: Here the ice is broken — who'll be round to play?

indicators.note: play means the letters move freely into a new order

parts.note: a round shape is the letter O

explanation.surface: At a party, someone breaks the ice by asking who will come round to play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to play' rearranges WHOLLBE with O. A seal or whale surfaces through a hole in the ice to breathe.
explanation.definitionFit: A breathing hole in sea ice, kept open by seals.

clue.text: Inaudible? That was heartbreak for Elvis

explanation.surface: Elvis could not be heard and was heartbroken.
explanation.walkthrough: The letter H is often silent, and its radio-alphabet codeword is this one; Heartbreak Hotel was an Elvis Presley hit.
explanation.definitionFit: The radio codeword for a letter often left unsounded; the setting of Presley's 1956 hit song.

clue.text: Sprinkles bactericide initially to get weeds out

indicators.note: initially means only the first letter of the following word is used
out signals the letters of weeds are put out of order

explanation.surface: A gardener sprays germ-killer to clear weeds.
explanation.definitionFit: To moisten with droplets, as morning dew does on grass.

clue.text: Duck! Soldiers are killed when they stand up

indicators.note: in a down clue, standing up means the pieces are read from bottom to top

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
to die is to be killed

explanation.surface: A warning shout: soldiers who stand up get shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when they stand up' turns REDIE upwards to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A large sea bird prized for its soft down.

clue.text: It could be right to take part

explanation.surface: Joining in could be the correct choice.
explanation.definitionFit: Right is one flank or face of something; to align with a faction is to back it in a dispute.

clue.text: He'll grow lethal to mice, it appears

definitions.text: He'll grow lethal to mice, it appears

indicators.note: it appears says the letters show themselves inside the words grow lethal

explanation.surface: A warning about some youngster who will grow up to be deadly to mice.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a whole, the clue describes a young bird that will grow into a mouse-killer, while the letters sit inside 'grow lethal'.
explanation.definitionFit: A young nocturnal raptor, which matures into a predator of mice.

clue.text: Play around and be indulgent, capturing child's heart

indicators.note: capturing means the first piece holds the second inside it

parts.note: to pander is to indulge someone's wishes

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle, dropping the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A permissive parent fools around, winning a child's heart.
explanation.definitionFit: To womanise is to flirt and have casual affairs.

clue.text: Fashionable person is an idiot — he's Arab, perhaps

parts.note: a clot is British slang for a fool
taken as written, without the apostrophe
an Arab is a breed of horse

explanation.surface: A trendsetter is mocked as a fool on an Arabian steed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who wears fashionable clothes as if a frame for displaying them.
